questions.question: If a² + b² + c² + 189 = 6 (a + 4b + 2c) , then sqrt{ab + bc + ca} is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any equation of form a² + b² + c² + k = 2(ma + nb + pc), the values are a = m, b = n, c = p.

Rewrite given RHS: 6(a + 4b + 2c) → 2(3a + 12b + 6c).

Directly identifying values: a = 3, b = 12, and c = 6.

Value = √(ab + bc + ca) = √(3 × 12 + 12 × 6 + 6 × 3) = √126.

√126 = √(9 × 14) = 3√14.

**∴ The correct answer is 3√14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: a² + b² + c² + 189 = 6a + 24b + 12c

Formula Used: (x − y)² = x² − 2xy + y²

⇒ a² − 6a + b² − 24b + c² − 12c + 189 = 0

⇒ (a² − 2 × 3a + 3²) + (b² − 2 × 12b + 12²) + (c² − 2 × 6c + 6²) + 189 − 9 − 144 − 36 = 0

⇒ (a − 3)² + (b − 12)² + (c − 6)² + 0 = 0

⇒ (a − 3)² + (b − 12)² + (c − 6)² = 0

⇒ Since sum of squares is zero, each base must be zero: a = 3, b = 12, c = 6

⇒ √(ab + bc + ca) = √(3 × 12 + 12 × 6 + 6 × 3) = √(36 + 72 + 18) = √126 = 3√14

**∴ The correct answer is 3√14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

If the sum of squares of real numbers is zero (x² + y² + z² = 0), then each individual term must be zero (x = 0, y = 0, z = 0).

Completing the Square

To convert x² + kx into a perfect square, add and subtract (k/2)² to get (x + k/2)² − (k/2)².

Square Root Simplification

For non-perfect squares, factor out the largest perfect square: √126 = √(9 × 14) = √9 × √14 = 3√14.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells an item for ₹430.5 after giving two successive discounts of 70% and 75% on its marked price. Had he not given any discount, he would have earned a profit of 40%. What is the cost price (in ₹) of the item?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective SP percentage of MP = (100 − 70)% × (100 − 75)% = 30% × 25% = 7.5%

Marked Price (MP) = 430.5 ÷ 7.5% = 430.5 ÷ 0.075 = 5740

When no discount is given, SP = MP = 5740, yielding 40% profit

Cost Price (CP) = MP ÷ (100% + 40%) = 5740 ÷ 1.4 = 4100

**∴ The correct answer is 4100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹430.5

Successive Discounts = 70% and 75%

Profit at no discount (at MP) = 40%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)

CP = MP ÷ (1 + Profit%/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09d1e56222cbf53b236d33105998c797ca3baaec04a4434b77bc6805f6fb2914.png] 

Let the Marked Price be MP.

⇒ 430.5 = MP × (1 − 70/100) × (1 − 75/100)

⇒ 430.5 = MP × (30/100) × (25/100)

⇒ 430.5 = MP × (3/10) × (1/4)

⇒ 430.5 = MP × (3/40)

⇒ MP = (430.5 × 40) ÷ 3

⇒ MP = 17220 ÷ 3 = 5740

If no discount is given, New SP = MP = 5740.

⇒ CP × (1 + 40/100) = 5740

⇒ CP × 1.4 = 5740

⇒ CP = 5740 ÷ 1.4

⇒ CP = 4100

**∴ The correct answer is 4100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

Total single discount equivalent to two successive discounts d₁ and d₂ is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂/100)%.

Relation between CP and MP

The ratio of CP to MP is given by CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%).

Marked Price Definition

Marked Price (List Price) is the price printed on the label. MP = CP + Markup.

questions.question: A solid metal sphere is melted and smaller spheres of equal radii are formed. 5% of the volume of the sphere is lost during the process. The smaller sphere has a radius that is one-tenth of the large sphere. If 14 liters of paint was needed to paint the larger sphere, how many liters is needed to paint all the smaller spheres?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Radius ratio R : r = 10 : 1 (as r = 1/10 R)

Volume ratio = 10³ : 1³ = 1000 : 1

Number of smaller spheres = 95% of 1000 = 950

Surface Area ratio for 1 sphere = 10² : 1² = 100 : 1

Total Area ratio = 100 : (950 × 1) = 1 : 9.5

Paint needed = 14 × 9.5 = 133 liters.

**∴ The correct answer is 133 liters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Radius of smaller sphere (r) = R/10 | Volume loss = 5% | Paint for large sphere = 14 liters

Formula: Volume of sphere = (4/3) × π × R³ | Surface Area = 4 × π × R²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21a5586f354f88d4c4e3e59796ce0f8da1acd993248f9e2f59d09142b3408bc4.png] 

⇒ Volume used = 95% of Large Sphere Volume

⇒ n × (4/3) × π × (R/10)³ = 0.95 × (4/3) × π × R³

⇒ n × (R³ / 1000) = 0.95 × R³

⇒ n = 0.95 × 1000 = 950 spheres

⇒ Area of Large sphere (AL) = 4 × π × R² = 14 units of paint

⇒ Area of one small sphere (Aₛ) = 4 × π × (R/10)² = (4 × π × R²) / 100 = AL / 100

⇒ Total Area of all small spheres = n × Aₛ = 950 × (AL / 100) = 9.5 × AL

⇒ Total paint needed = 9.5 × 14 = 133 liters

**∴ The correct answer is 133 liters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume and Surface Area of Sphere

The volume of a sphere is V = (4/3)πr³ and the curved surface area is A = 4πr².

Melting and Recasting Rule

When a solid is melted to form new solids, the total volume remains constant unless there is a specific loss mentioned (Vᵢₙᵢₜᵢₐₗ = Vfᵢₙₐₗ + Loss).

Scaling Properties

If the linear dimensions (radius) of a shape are changed by a factor k, the area changes by k² and the volume changes by k³.

questions.question: Which of the following processes is responsible for the transportation of soluble products formed by photosynthesis in different parts of plant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Translocation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Translocation** is the process by which soluble products of **photosynthesis**, such as sugars (primarily **sucrose**) and amino acids, are transported from the leaves (the source) to other parts of the plant like roots, fruits, and growing seeds (the sinks).
 
• This transport occurs through a specialized vascular tissue known as the **Phloem**. Unlike water transport, translocation is an active process that requires **ATP** (energy).
 
• **Transpiration** is the process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts, such as leaves, stems, and flowers. It primarily involves the **Xylem** and helps in the upward movement of water and minerals.
 
• **Assimilation** refers to the biological process where the nutrients absorbed and transported are actually utilized by the cells to build new protoplasm or produce energy.
 
• **Termination** is a term generally used in genetics or molecular biology to describe the end of a process like **DNA replication**, **transcription**, or **translation**, and is not a transport mechanism in plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Phloem** consists of **sieve tubes** and **companion cells** which facilitate the bulk flow of organic solutes.
 
• While the movement in the **Xylem** is strictly **unidirectional** (upwards from roots to leaves), the movement in the **Phloem** is **multidirectional**, allowing food to reach all parts of the plant based on their metabolic needs.
 
• The **Pressure Flow Hypothesis** (or Munch hypothesis) is the most accepted theory explaining how translocation works, suggesting that high **osmotic pressure** in the phloem at the source pushes the sap toward the sink.
 
• Environmental factors like **temperature** and **light intensity** can indirectly affect the rate of translocation by influencing the rate of photosynthesis.

Ratio Substitution Property

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

questions.question: The cost of 7 kg of sugar of quality A is ₹245, and the cost of 5 kg of sugar of quality B is ₹300. In what ratio should quality A sugar and quality B sugar be mixed so that the cost of 1 kg of the mixture is ₹50?

questions.question: For an echo to be heard clearly, the reflecting surface should be at least how far from the listener? (Take speed of sound ≈ 340 m/s)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17 m**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **echo** is the repetition of sound caused by the **reflection** of sound waves from a hard surface back to the listener.
 
• To hear a distinct echo, the sensation of the original sound must have died out in our brain. The human brain retains any sound for approximately **0.1 seconds**; this is known as the **persistence of hearing**.
 
• For the original sound and the reflected sound to be perceived as separate, the reflected sound must reach the ear at least **0.1 seconds** after the original sound.
 
• Total distance traveled by the sound (from source to obstacle and back) can be calculated using the formula: **Total Distance = Speed × Time**.
 
• Let **d** be the distance between the listener and the reflecting surface. The total distance traveled by the sound is **2d**.
 
• Using the given **speed of sound (340 m/s)** and the minimum time required **(0.1 s)**:

 2d = 340 m/s × 0.1 s

 2d = 34 m

 d = 34 / 2 = **17 m**.
 
• Therefore, the reflecting surface must be at a minimum distance of **17 m** for an echo to be heard clearly. If the distance is shorter, the reflected sound arrives before 0.1 seconds and merges with the original sound, creating **reverberation** instead of a distinct echo.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **speed of sound** in air is not constant; it increases with an increase in **temperature** and **humidity**. Therefore, the minimum distance for an echo might change slightly depending on environmental conditions.
 
• **Reverberation** is the persistence of sound in a closed enclosure due to multiple reflections even after the source has stopped. This is commonly observed in large concert halls or empty rooms.
 
• Reflection of sound follows the same laws as the **reflection of light**: the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection, and they all lie in the same plane.
 
• The principle of echo is utilized in **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) to determine the depth of seas or to locate underwater objects like shoals of fish, shipwrecks, or enemy submarines.
 
• Animals like **bats** and **dolphins** use **echolocation** to navigate and find prey by emitting high-frequency ultrasonic waves and listening to the echoes.

questions.question: The cilia in the upper respiratory tract primarily help in:

options.text: Removing harmful particles from inhaled air

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Removing harmful particles from inhaled air**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cilia** are microscopic, hair-like structures that line the **respiratory tract**, including the nasal cavity, trachea, and bronchi.
 
• Their primary function is to act as a defense mechanism by moving in a coordinated, wave-like rhythm to sweep **mucus** toward the pharynx.
 
• This process is known as the **mucociliary escalator**. The mucus traps inhaled **dust**, **bacteria**, **viruses**, and other foreign **pollutants**, and the cilia move this contaminated mucus away from the lungs to be swallowed or expelled through coughing or sneezing.
 
• **Pumping blood** is the function of the **heart**, not the respiratory cilia.
 
• **Absorbing oxygen** and **gas exchange** occur deep within the lungs in the **alveoli**, where the air-blood barrier is thin enough for diffusion to take place. Cilia are not involved in the chemical process of gas exchange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cigarette smoke contains chemicals that can **paralyze** or destroy **cilia**, which is why chronic smokers often develop a 'smoker's cough' as their body struggles to clear mucus without the help of functional cilia.
 
• **Goblet cells** are specialized cells located alongside ciliated cells that produce the sticky **mucus** required to trap particles.
 
• **Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD)** is a rare genetic disorder where the cilia do not move correctly, leading to chronic respiratory infections and lung damage.
 
• The upper respiratory tract consists of the **nose**, **nasal cavity**, **pharynx**, and **larynx**, while the lower tract includes the **trachea**, **bronchi**, and **lungs**.

questions.question: If the energy of an electron in the second orbit of hydrogen is −3.4 eV, what is the energy in the fourth orbit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**−0.85 eV**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Bohr's atomic model**, the energy of an electron in the nth orbit of a **Hydrogen atom** is given by the formula: Eₙ = (-13.6)/(n²⁾ eV, where **n** is the **principal quantum number** (orbit number).
 
• The relationship shows that energy is **inversely proportional to the square** of the orbit number ( E propto (1)/(n²⁾ ).
 
• For the **second orbit (n = 2)**, the energy is: E₂ = (-13.6)/(2²⁾ = (-13.6)/(4) = -3.4 eV. This matches the value provided in the question.
 
• To find the energy in the **fourth orbit (n = 4)**, we substitute n = 4 into the formula: E₄ = (-13.6)/(4²⁾ = (-13.6)/(16) .
 
• Dividing -13.6 by 16 gives **-0.85 eV**.
 
• Alternatively, since the orbit number increased from 2 to 4 (it doubled), and energy depends on the inverse square of n, the energy becomes 1/4th of the value at n = 2: **-3.4 / 4 = -0.85 eV**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **ground state energy** (n = 1) for a hydrogen atom is **-13.6 eV**.
 
• The **negative sign** in the energy equation indicates that the electron is in a **bound state** with the nucleus; it requires external energy to be removed.
 
• The **Ionization Energy** of hydrogen is 13.6 eV, which is the energy required to move an electron from the ground state (n = 1) to infinity (n = ∞).
 
• As the value of **n increases**, the energy levels become **closer together** and the total energy becomes less negative (approaches zero).
 
• Energy levels summary: **n=1 is -13.6 eV**, **n=2 is -3.4 eV**, **n=3 is -1.51 eV**, and **n=4 is -0.85 eV**.

questions.question: The distance between the pole and the principal focus of a spherical mirror is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Focal length**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **focal length** is the distance between the **pole (P)** of the spherical mirror and its **principal focus (F)**. It is represented by the letter **'f'**.
 
• The **radius of curvature (R)** is the distance from the **pole** to the **center of curvature (C)**. It represents the radius of the hollow sphere from which the mirror was cut.
 
• The relationship between the radius of curvature and the focal length for a mirror with a small aperture is **R = 2f** (or f = R / 2).
 
• **Magnification (m)** is the ratio of the **height of the image** to the **height of the object**. It is a dimensionless quantity that indicates how much larger or smaller the image is compared to the object.
 
• **Aperture** is the **effective diameter** of the light-reflecting area of the spherical mirror. It determines how much light is captured by the mirror to form an image.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **pole** is the geometric center of the reflecting spherical surface.
 
• The **principal axis** is the imaginary straight line passing through both the **pole** and the **center of curvature**.
 
• In a **concave mirror**, the principal focus is a point on the principal axis where light rays parallel to the axis actually **converge** after reflection.
 
• In a **convex mirror**, the principal focus is a point from which light rays parallel to the axis **appear to diverge** after reflection.
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the focal length of a **concave mirror** is **negative**, while the focal length of a **convex mirror** is **positive**.

questions.question: Megaphones, loudhailers, horns and musical instruments like trumpets and shehnais are designed to:

options.text: Spread sound equally in all directions
Send sound in a specific direction

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Send sound in a specific direction**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Megaphones**, **loudhailers**, **horns**, and musical instruments like **trumpets** and **shehnais** are all designed with a **conical** or funnel-like shape.
 
• The primary function of this design is to ensure that sound waves are guided by **multiple reflections** within the tube or cone towards the opening.
 
• Instead of allowing sound to spread out and dissipate in all directions, these instruments **concentrate the sound energy** and direct it along a **specific path** or direction.
 
• By restricting the spread of sound, the **amplitude** of the sound waves remains higher over a longer distance in that particular direction, making the sound appear louder to an observer located in front of the instrument.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sound** is a **longitudinal wave** that requires a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel.
 
• The phenomenon of **reflection of sound** follows the same laws as the reflection of light, where the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
 
• A **stethoscope** is another medical instrument that works on the principle of **multiple reflections** of sound to hear the internal sounds of the human body, such as heartbeats.
 
• The **intensity** of sound is defined as the sound power per unit area, and by narrowing the area through which sound travels (using a horn), the intensity in that specific direction is significantly increased.

questions.question: The mean of a data is four times of its mode. If the median of the data is 63, find its mean.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Empirical Relation: 3 × Median = 2 × Mean + Mode

Given Mean = 4 × Mode ⇒ Mode = Mean / 4

3 × 63 = 2 × Mean + Mean / 4

189 = 9/4 × Mean

Mean = (189 × 4) / 9 = 84

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Median = 63

Mean = 4 × Mode

Formula used: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/adf9eabd5295fbb782da874f681b601c17d515851f764b276fb79d19a1bf7cb0.png] 

Let Mode = x, then Mean = 4x

⇒ Mode = 3 × 63 − 2 × (4x)

⇒ x = 189 − 8x

⇒ x + 8x = 189

⇒ 9x = 189

⇒ x = 189 ÷ 9

⇒ x = 21

⇒ Mean = 4 × 21 = 84

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

For moderately asymmetrical distributions, the relationship is Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the values of Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal.

Positional vs Mathematical Averages

Mean is a mathematical average (sensitive to every value), while Median and Mode are positional averages.

questions.question: On the basis of function, the plasma membrane is ________ in nature.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**selectively permeable**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **plasma membrane**, also known as the cell membrane, is described as **selectively permeable** because it regulates the entry and exit of molecules, allowing only certain substances to pass through while blocking others.
 
• This selective nature is functional; it enables the cell to maintain a constant internal environment (**homeostasis**) by controlling the concentration of ions, nutrients, and waste products.
 
• **Semi-permeable** membranes typically allow only the solvent (usually water) to pass through, whereas a **selectively permeable** membrane like the plasma membrane can choose specific solutes to transport via active or passive mechanisms.
 
• A **fully permeable** membrane, such as the **cell wall** in plants, allows all substances to pass through without any selection.
 
• A **fully non-permeable** membrane would completely isolate the cell, preventing it from obtaining nutrients or discarding waste, which would lead to cell death.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The structure of the plasma membrane is best explained by the **Fluid Mosaic Model**, proposed by **S.J. Singer** and **G.L. Nicolson** in **1972**.
 
• It is primarily composed of a **phospholipid bilayer** with embedded **proteins**, **cholesterol**, and **carbohydrates**.
 
• Substances move across the membrane through **Passive Transport** (like simple diffusion and facilitated diffusion) which requires no energy, and **Active Transport** (using **ATP**) to move molecules against a concentration gradient.
 
• The membrane proteins act as **channels**, **pumps**, or **receptors**, which are vital for cell signaling and material exchange.

questions.question: A student's marks were incorrectly entered as 44 instead of 92. Due to this, the avarage marks of the class got decreased by (4)/(3) . What is the number of students in the class?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total difference in marks = Correct marks − Incorrect marks = 92 − 44 = 48.

Decrease in average marks = 4/3.

Number of students = Total marks difference ÷ Change in average.

Number of students = 48 ÷ (4/3) ⇒ 48 × 3 ÷ 4 = 12 × 3 = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Actual marks = 92

Incorrectly entered marks = 44

Decrease in average = 4/3

**Formula Used:**

Number of students = (Error in total sum) ÷ (Change in average)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/25dd1a8d481af23b65bc27f77128853b22d457d5a61c34b809978b33fd8822e6.png] 

⇒ Let the number of students be N.

⇒ Error in total marks = 92 − 44 = 48

⇒ Since the average decreased by 4/3 when marks were reduced by 48, we equate the total change:

⇒ Total change in marks = N × (Change in Average)

⇒ 48 = N × (4/3)

⇒ N = (48 × 3) ÷ 4

⇒ N = 144 ÷ 4

⇒ N = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corrected Average Concept

Correct Average = (Incorrect Sum + Correct value − Incorrect value) ÷ Number of items.

Net Deviation Rule

In any average calculation, the sum of deviations from the average is always zero. Error in sum = Total change in average × Total number of observations.

Effect of Adding an Item

If a new value X is added to N items with average A, the new average = (N × A + X) ÷ (N + 1).

Arithmetic Mean

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between mean, median, and mode is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

questions.question: Anand purchased an item and spent ₹63 on its repair. He then sold it to Bharath at a profit of 25%. Later, Bharath sold the item for ₹8415, incurring a loss of 15%. What was Anand’s cost (in ₹) of the item just before selling it to Bharath?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Bharath SP = ₹8415 at 15% loss → 85% = 8415

Bharath CP (Anand SP) = 8415 ÷ 0.85 = ₹9900

Anand Total CP at 25% profit → 125% = 9900

Anand Total CP = 9900 ÷ 1.25 = ₹7920

**∴ The correct answer is 7920.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Bharath Selling Price (SPB) = ₹8415

Bharath Loss% = 15%

Anand Profit% = 25%

Formula: CP = SP × [100 / (100 ± Profit/Loss%)]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d686563923bbbba1000b047a5b243a1ba62504a6515e858c5fca842db3ebb9c.png] ⇒ Cost Price for Bharath = 8415 × [100 / (100 − 15)] ⇒ Cost Price for Bharath = 8415 × (100 / 85) = ₹9900 ⇒ Selling Price for Anand = Cost Price for Bharath = ₹9900 ⇒ Total Cost Price for Anand = 9900 × [100 / (100 + 25)] ⇒ Total Cost Price for Anand = 9900 × (100 / 125) ⇒ Total Cost Price for Anand = 9900 × 0.8 ⇒ Total Cost Price for Anand = ₹7920

**∴ The correct answer is 7920.**

Total Cost Price Calculation

Total CP = Purchasing Price + Overhead Expenses (Repair, Transport, etc.). Profit or loss is always calculated on the Total CP.

Successive Percentage Change

When multiple profit/loss transactions occur, the net change can be calculated as CP × (100±P1/100) × (100±P2/100) = Final SP.

Effective Profit/Loss

Effective percentage = a + b + (ab/100), where profit is positive and loss is negative.
